scenes.headline: How one week of security news fits together
scenes.sub: Weak CA keys, PHP bugs, a poisoned LiteLLM, and leaked platform secrets.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Vellum! Broken certificate keys, two PHP bugs, a poisoned AI gateway release, and leaked platform secrets. Here's how they fit.

scenes.text: Patch by who is exploiting it and who can reach it, not by the CVSS number alone.
scenes.mark: who is exploiting it and who can reach it
scenes.say: The idea: rank by who is exploiting a bug and who can reach it, not by CVSS alone.

scenes.title: Why a weak intermediate key matters

steps.say: A trusted root signs an intermediate, whose private key should be a huge random number.
These keys were tiny. Anyone could recompute one and sign a certificate for any site.
Browsers pushed blocklists within hours. Software with its own trust store needs an update.

scenes.title: Where the PHP bugs live
scenes.say: The two PHP bugs sit in how a worker handles requests.

items.say: A request arrives, and PHP sets up its internal state.
An error stops the request part way through.
Cleanup, or the next request on that worker, trusts memory that is half-built or already freed.
The fixed releases reset that state. Restart every worker, or the old code keeps running.

scenes.title: How a poisoned release reaches you
scenes.say: LiteLLM shipped a malicious release. Here is its path.

items.say: Attackers held stolen developer credentials with release access.
They pointed the release workflow at a lookalike repository.
The wheels and Docker images, including latest, were out for about two hours.
Planted files run whenever Python starts, so installing was enough.

scenes.title: Two ways to order the list

left.title: By CVSS
left.say: Sorting by CVSS puts the scariest worst case first.

right.title: By real-world risk
right.say: Sorting by risk asks: is it exploited, does it need a login, can the internet reach it?

scenes.label: the published CVSS for both PHP bugs, not the leaked 10.0
scenes.say: The leak said ten. Both PHP bugs are published at nine point two.

scenes.text: Update, restart, rotate. A patched file protects nothing until the process is new, and a leaked key works until rotated.
scenes.mark: a leaked key works until rotated
scenes.say: Update, restart, and rotate. A patched file protects nothing until the process is new. A leaked key keeps working until you rotate it.

recap: Weak keys break the chain of trust
Pin releases and rotate leaked secrets
scenes.say: Weak keys break trust. Pin releases, rotate secrets. Rank by exploitation and reach.
